subject: Manually setting population colours in PCoA plots

messages.author: 839e964952da202f
messages.subject: Manually setting population colours in PCoA plots
parts:
Hi there,
Just wondering if there was a way to manually set colours attributed to different populations in a PCoA plot generated by gl.pcoa.plot()? 
Thanks!
Bonnie

messages.author: 8559f272679693c3
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Manually setting population colours in PCoA plots
parts:
Hi Bonnie,

 

I’m hardly a pro at this, but I like to use the s.class function to plot my PCA results and also to add the legend. It allows better customisation IMO.

 

For example:

 

plot.new() #clear old plots. pca1 in the next step is the output of the gl.pcoa function

s.class(pca1$scores, pop(your.gl), clabel=0, cpoint=2, grid=TRUE, axesell=FALSE, addaxes=TRUE, col=your.colours.cheme) # there are lots of ways of setting your colours. You could just add “col=rainbow”, or you could have previously set a particular colour gradient by e.g.

# #make a gradient of colours suiting N sites

#load(colorRamps) # a useful package

#NS.col <- colorRamps::blue2red(17) #17 hues on the blue-red spectrum

#then when plotting above you’d add “col=NS.col”

 

#add a legend

legend(xy.coords(x=c(-10,-3), y=c(0,4)), pch=19, pt.cex=2, bty="n", levels(pop(your.gl)), ncol=3, y.intersp=0.5, x.intersp=0.5, col=NS.col,

 

add.scatter.eig(pca1$eig[1:20],2,1,1, ratio=0.2)#add the scree plot

 

Good luck.

 

Olly

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Manually setting population colours in PCoA plots
parts:
Hi Bonnie,

 

As the gl.pcoa function is a simple wrapper around the glPca function from adegenet. A good way to start to customise is to use the return object of gl.pcoa and use the code provided in the adegenet tutorials to customise scripts.

 

Finally another way in case you do not know is to plot the pcoa and then under windows (and Mac? Not sure) export it as an image and save it as a metafile (emf). You can edit this kind of image in word/powerpoint (right-click and ungroup).

 

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.subject: Re: Manually setting population colours in PCoA plots
parts:
Hi Bonnie and Andrzej,

Just an alternate approach to those already given.

dartR was written for input and exploratory analysis, and we were keen not to fall into the trap of duplicating functions that were already available in R.

So my advice would be to grab the associated data important for your plotting

indNames(gl)
popNames(gl)

and the coordinates of the points

pcoa <- gl.pcoa(gl,nfactors=2)
pcoa$scores

bundle them into a dataframe

df <- data.frame(id=indNames(gl),pop=popNames(gl),pcoa$scores)

and then use ggplot or any R plotting packages you are familiar with to produce the plots you require.

Might be some minor syntax errors in the above, as I am not close to a computer.

Arthur

messages.subject: Re: Manually setting population colours in PCoA plots
parts:
Hi Bonnie,

The latest function, gl.pcoa.plot() -- attached -- now has the option to output the individual labels, population labels and pcoa scores so you can plot these using the full power of ggplot or similar.

Set the parameter plot.out. If TRUE, the function returns a plot object compatible with ggplot, otherwise returns a dataframe that can be used to plot independently using ggplot [default TRUE]

Hope this helps,

A
